open_assumptions: The journal log, known islands and rumor offers travel in the player's private status as a JSON string, a JSON string and `type:offer` pairs, not nested Schema collections.
Leads go out as a new `journal` message type (the reveals keep their `reveal` messages); purchase answers are `rumor-result`, one per request, with a merged pending retry getting no separate answer.
A request outside play (lobby or after the end) is refused `not-in-play` at once and not recorded; `busy` is not recorded either.
A player waiting to respawn is refused `not-at-dock` even when its ship still sits at a dock; a player grappled while moored is refused `player-in-duel`.
Sighting and no-lead journal entries stay `active`: the design takes the resolved status only from `rumor-resolved`.
The `none` offer covers both intel's `capped` and `none` answers (the button reads 'no lead to sell now').

Existing tests changed: the fruit and web 'protocol v9' tests now assert >= 9 (v10 is asserted in the new journal tests), and rubbings.test.ts's §16 wire check now scans state frames only, ignoring the guest's own `"type":"sun"` journal JSON and `sun:<offer>` strings.
